zh.question: 一个微生物被风带到窗台上，就一定能在那里越长越多吗？
zh.observe: 依次选择土壤、水、皮肤和空气，打开想象放大镜。比较每处的水分、营养和运输线索，分清到达、存活与繁殖三件事。

academic.title: 微生物是观察尺度，不是单一谱系
academic.body: 日常所说微生物包括细菌、古菌、显微真菌、许多原生生物和微型藻类等不同类群；病毒也常在微生物学中研究，但它不是细胞生物。它们的结构、能量来源和生活方式差别很大，不能把一个彩色椭圆当作所有微生物的共同身体。这里不同场景的图形只提醒存在多样性，不承担物种鉴定或真实数量统计。

academic.title: 广泛分布来自分散与环境筛选
academic.body: 水、风、尘粒和动物活动可以搬运微生物或孢子，但被运到一处只代表到达。能否保持活性或存活，取决于干燥、辐射、温度等压力；能否繁殖，还需要适合的水分、能源、营养和化学环境。一些微生物能以休眠或耐受形式等待条件改变。因此“几乎到处都能发现”不等于“每一种都在每个地方大量生长”。

academic.title: 微小空间也有不同的群落
academic.body: 土粒孔隙中的含水量、氧和有机质分布并不均一，皮肤的湿润、干燥和多油区域也常有不同群落。群落成员通过竞争、互利和物质交换相互影响，一些参与分解与元素循环。检测到微生物或其 DNA 不等于它正在活跃繁殖，更不自动等于健康危害；需要进一步判断种类、活性、位置和接触方式。

zh.misconception: “到处都有微生物”不表示每一种都能到处生长，也不表示每次遇到微生物都会生病。
zh.boundary: 想象放大镜不是实测显微图；场景内形状、颜色、比例与数量是示意，不能用清澈程度或这些图标判断卫生状况。

narration.label: 眼睛看不到的邻居
narration.text: 抓一把土、望一望池水，再看看自己的手，许多地方都可能有很小的微生物。它们往往小得让眼睛看不清，所以我们准备了一面想象放大镜。里面的颜色和形状是帮助理解的画，不是刚刚从你手上拍到的照片。先从土里开始，找找颗粒之间的小空间。
narration.cue: 选土壤并打开想象放大镜。

narration.label: 不同地方，不同小家
narration.text: 土粒之间可能有水、空气和养分。一些微生物在这里参与分解落叶。再换到池水和皮肤，看看周围条件哪里不同。我们停一停，想想干燥的地方和湿润的地方，会不会适合完全相同的小生物？就算都在皮肤上，不同位置也可能有不同的邻居。
narration.cue: 比较土壤、水、皮肤，在干湿差异处停三秒。

narration.label: 搭便车不等于住下来
narration.text: 现在看看空气。有些微生物或者孢子，会跟着尘粒、飞沫和气流移动，像搭了一段便车。可是到了新地方，不一定能住下来，更不一定能越来越多。那里如果太干、没有合适的食物，或者条件不对，它们就可能无法生长。到达、活下来和长出更多，是三件不同的事。
narration.cue: 选空气，强调少量随颗粒运输的代表。

narration.label: 好奇，也要分清楚
narration.text: 微生物里有很多不同成员，不能全部叫作细菌，也不能全部当成病菌。水看起来很清，也不告诉我们里面有什么；看见一个图标，更不能判断真实数量。我们今天练习的是带着问题观察：它在哪里，靠什么生活，到了这里还能不能长？把这些问题分开，小小世界就清楚一些了。
narration.cue: 依次回顾四场景，最后收起想象放大镜。

en.question: If a microbe reaches a windowsill on the wind, must it multiply there?
en.observe: Inspect soil, water, skin and air using the imagined magnifier. Compare water, nutrients and transport clues, separating arrival, survival and growth.

academic.title: Microbes are not one evolutionary group
academic.body: Microbial life includes bacteria, archaea, microscopic fungi and many protists and algae. Viruses are also studied in microbiology but are not cellular organisms. Their structures and energy sources differ greatly. Coloured shapes here suggest diversity rather than providing species identification or population counts.

academic.title: Dispersal is followed by environmental filtering
academic.body: Air, water, dust and animals can transport microbes or spores. Arrival does not establish survival, and survival does not establish growth. Drying, radiation and temperature impose stresses, while reproduction requires suitable resources and chemistry. Some organisms persist in dormant or resistant forms until conditions change.

academic.title: Small habitats support different communities
academic.body: Soil pores differ in moisture, oxygen and organic material, while skin sites differ in moisture and oils. Community members compete and exchange resources, with some contributing to decomposition and nutrient cycles. Detecting organisms or DNA alone does not demonstrate active growth or a health hazard; identity, activity and context matter.

en.misconception: Widespread microbes do not mean every kind grows everywhere or that every encounter causes illness.
en.boundary: The imagined lens is not measured microscopy. Shapes, colours, sizes and counts are illustrative, and neither clarity nor these symbols establish hygiene or safety.

narration.label: Neighbours too small to see
narration.text: Soil, pond water and our skin can all contain tiny microbes. Our eyes usually cannot inspect them directly, so we have an imagined magnifying lens. Its colours and shapes are explanatory drawings, not photographs of your hand. Begin in soil and look between the grains.
narration.cue: Choose soil and open the imagined lens.

narration.label: Different tiny homes
narration.text: Spaces in soil can hold air, water and nutrients, and some microbes help decompose leaves. Compare pond water and skin next. Pause and ask whether a dry place and a wet place would suit exactly the same organisms. Even different regions of skin can support different neighbours.
narration.cue: Compare soil, water and skin, then pause.

narration.label: A ride does not make a home
narration.text: Some microbes or spores travel with dust, droplets and moving air. Reaching somewhere new does not mean settling successfully or multiplying. The place may be too dry or lack suitable resources. Arrival, survival and growth are three different things.
narration.cue: Choose air and show a few transported representatives.

narration.label: Stay curious and make distinctions
narration.text: Microbes include many different groups, not just bacteria or disease-causing organisms. Clear-looking water does not reveal what lives in it, and an icon cannot measure a population. Ask where an organism is, what supports it and whether it can grow there. Separating those questions makes this tiny world easier to understand.
narration.cue: Review the four habitats and close the imagined lens.

references.title: Microbiology Society — Microbes and where to find them
